title: Sections of a finite constant pro-etale sheaf as continuous functions
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $V\to X$ be an object of the small pro-etale site with its small skeleton [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Give $A$ the discrete topology (every subset is open). The constant sheaf of rings $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] has canonical ring isomorphisms
$$\theta_{X,V}:A_X(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(|V|,A),$$
where $|V|$ is the underlying Zariski space and $C(|V|,A)$ is the ring of continuous functions with pointwise operations. These isomorphisms send the image of every constant-presheaf element $a\in A$ to the constant function with value $a$. For every morphism $h:W\to V$ of objects of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and every $s\in A_X(V)$ they satisfy $\theta_{X,W}(h^*s)=\theta_{X,V}(s)\circ|h|$. No quasi-compactness, connectedness or nonemptiness assumption is imposed on $X$ or $V$.

proof.text: For each object V of X_proet put L_A(V)=C(|V|,A), with restrictions by precomposition. The finite commutative ring A with its discrete topology is in particular a topological abelian group whose addition and negation are continuous. The existing Mathlib leaf [lem-cbc-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf] therefore says that U maps to C(|U|,A), with pointwise addition, is an fpqc sheaf on schemes. By the covering clause of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], every pro-etale covering {U_i to U} is an fpqc covering of schemes; by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change] each fibre product U_i x_U U_j is weakly etale over X (base change of U_i to U, then composition with U to X), so it is (isomorphic to) an object of X_proet and the matching conditions for the covering in X_proet and in schemes coincide. Hence the restriction of this presheaf to X_proet is a sheaf of abelian groups. Pointwise multiplication and the constant function 1 preserve continuity and restrictions, and the sheaf condition concerns only the underlying sets, so L_A is a sheaf of commutative rings.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, printed p. 30, continuous-function sheaf assertion; the fpqc sheaf formulation is the Mathlib leaf

proof.text: The map of presheaves phi: P_A to L_A from the constant presheaf P_A(V)=A sends a to the constant function with value a; it is a map of presheaves of commutative rings because the operations of L_A are pointwise. If f in L_A(V), then for each a in the finite set A the fibre V_a=f^{-1}({a}) is open because A is discrete, and it is also closed because its complement is the finite union of the other open fibres. Thus the finitely many fibres are clopen and cover |V|; the intersection of V_a with an affine open Spec R of V is clopen in Spec R, hence of the form Spec R_e for an idempotent e, so affine. Each open immersion V_a to V is flat and a monomorphism, so its diagonal is an isomorphism and it is weakly etale; by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change] the composite V_a to V to X is weakly etale, so V_a is an object of X_proet. For every affine open W of V the finitely many affine opens W meet V_a cover W, so {V_a to V} is a pro-etale covering by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], on whose members f restricts to the constant a. Thus phi is locally surjective. It is locally injective: two constants that agree on a nonempty object have equal values, while on the empty object the empty family is a covering. The universal property of ring-valued sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] gives a unique map of sheaves of rings theta: A_X to L_A from the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] with theta eta = phi, eta the sheafification unit. By [lem-pe-ring-sheafification-underlying-sets] the underlying set map of eta is a set-valued sheafification of the underlying presheaf of sets of P_A. By [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] the set-sheafification of the locally surjective and locally injective map phi is an isomorphism; since L_A is already a sheaf its own unit is an isomorphism, and uniqueness of factorization through the set-valued unit identifies the underlying set map of theta with this isomorphism. Hence theta is bijective on every object, and as each component is a ring homomorphism, theta is an isomorphism of sheaves of rings.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, printed p. 30, discrete-space assertion and constant-section normalization; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 0F6D supporting the pro-etale covering context

proof.text: The presheaf map phi preserves addition, multiplication, and one, because these operations are pointwise and constant functions have the corresponding constant values; so the isomorphism theta of the previous step is a canonical ring isomorphism, and theta eta = phi says that it sends the image of every constant-presheaf element a to the constant function a. For a morphism h:W to V in X_proet, theta is a morphism of sheaves, so theta_W(h^*s)=h^*theta_V(s)=theta_V(s) composed with |h|, since the restriction in L_A is precomposition by the underlying scheme map. This argument is objectwise and uses neither quasi-compactness nor connectedness nor nonemptiness; the empty object is covered by the empty family as above.

split_report.summary: Split the imported statement into three proof steps. First, the existing Mathlib fpqc sheaf of continuous functions restricts to a pro-etale sheaf and gains pointwise ring operations. Second, finite discrete fibres give a pro-etale covering by open fibres, so the constant presheaf map is locally bijective and sheafification yields the canonical isomorphism. Third, pointwise operations, constant-section normalization, and restriction naturality give the ring and pullback clauses, including empty and disconnected cases.
